definitions.explanation: Medicine taken to relieve constipation. The everyday, consumer-facing word — packaging at pharmacies and TV ads typically use this term rather than the medical {下剤|げざい}.

examples.japanese: {便秘薬|べんぴやく}を{飲|の}んだ。
{薬局|やっきょく}で{便秘薬|べんぴやく}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a laxative at the pharmacy.

examples.japanese: {便秘薬|べんぴやく}は{毎日|まいにち}{使|つか}わずに、{食生活|しょくせいかつ}の{改善|かいぜん}を{先|さき}にしたほうがいい。
examples.english: Rather than using a laxative every day, it's better to improve your diet first.

notes:
{便秘|べんぴ} (constipation) + {薬|やく} (medicine). The everyday consumer term — pharmacy shelves and TV commercials use this rather than the medical-register {下剤|げざい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {便秘薬|べんぴやく}を{飲|の}む: to take a laxative
- {便秘薬|べんぴやく}に{頼|たよ}る: to rely on laxatives
- {市販|しはん}の{便秘薬|べんぴやく}: over-the-counter laxative

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {下剤|げざい}: laxative — medical register; used in clinical contexts
- {整腸|せいちょう}{剤|ざい}: digestive-regulating medicine — broader, also for diarrhea
- {便秘|べんぴ}: constipation (the condition itself)
